idiom_name: dashmap shards (with_shard_amount) / Vec<Mutex<..>> for custom state
implementation_notes: dashmap implements the pattern for maps: a DashMap is an array of shards, each a CachePadded<RwLock<HashMap>>, and the key's hash selects the shard (with_shard_amount fixes the shard count; determine_shard exposes the mapping; into_shards hands over the raw shard array). Its guard types (Ref/RefMut) hold the shard lock, so compound per-key operations serialize per shard instead of globally. For keyed state that is not a map - files, connections, sessions - the manual realization is a Vec<Mutex<T>> plus a hash function, with parking_lot::Mutex as the common non-poisoning alternative to std::sync::Mutex.
pitfalls: Holding a dashmap Ref or RefMut while calling back into the same map deadlocks the shard; take the value out or finish the computation before dropping the guard.

std::sync::Mutex poisoning turns one panicking stripe holder into panics in all later lock().unwrap() calls; decide explicitly between unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner) and parking_lot::Mutex, which has no poisoning.
Shard locks give no cross-shard atomicity: an operation spanning two keys can see them in different shards and is not atomic as a whole.
